### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**21** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `owner_id (literal, 31 pages)`
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **153** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **153**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **98** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **136** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3bd28e2b2ea81206dc9f5507de205b564bd97097` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `265043e56f71d6a4a64e522fd3d0388c51e42478` — the merge of head `a0360aad8cdfb17203cb9c6ca7adab17c88dd3b3` into base `3bd28e2b2ea81206dc9f5507de205b564bd97097`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 265043e56f71d6a4a64e522fd3d0388c51e42478 && git checkout 265043e56f71d6a4a64e522fd3d0388c51e42478
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3bd28e2b2ea81206dc9f5507de205b564bd97097 a0360aad8cdfb17203cb9c6ca7adab17c88dd3b3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3bd28e2b2ea81206dc9f5507de205b564bd97097 && git merge --no-ff a0360aad8cdfb17203cb9c6ca7adab17c88dd3b3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3bd28e2b2ea81206dc9f5507de205b564bd97097
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b1c9143f9ede26bfb8cea990f1b43cb86ac2ba38`

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept/refuse sets: unchanged at every door.** No door schema is touched (diff files: `conversions/registry.ts`, `ui/filter-rule-array.ts` + its test, two semantic entries, `migrations/registry.ts`, the new test, one changeset). The conversion is `retiredFromLoadPath: true` (`packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts:10531`), `applyConversions` skips it on the authoring funnel (`conversions/apply.ts:132`), and §7 of the new test pins that `normalizeStackInput` leaves `{ stage: 'open' }` unconverted and un-noticed. Right. Only refusal TEXT moves, and only for combinator records (next bullet).
- **Refusal text confined to combinator records.** Probe on a throwaway worktree of the head, base `84880f92` `filter-rule-array.ts` loaded beside head, same `ViewFilterRuleSchema`, 17 inputs: `identical=14 changed=3`. Identical: flat, `{}`, null value, operator object, 4 keys, array value, `$text`, string, number, AST, `Date`, a rule array with a bad member, `$OR` (uppercase), `$nor`. Changed: `$or` alone, `$and`+`$not` beside a field, `$and` beside 4 fields. Code `invalid_type` and path `filter` unchanged in all three. Mechanism: `combinators` is read from `LOGICAL_OPERATORS` (`ui/filter-rule-array.ts:163-164`); with none, `fields === authored` and `lead` is the historic sentence byte for byte (`:181-183`). Right, and wider than the dev's 11/11.
- **Conversion input→output, measured (55-case probe, `collectConversionNotices` with `includeRetired`).** Converted: flat scalars incl. `''`, `0`, `false`; dotted field `owner.name`; placeholders/macros verbatim; `{ f: { $ne: null } }` → `not_equals null`; `{ f: { $eq: null } }` → `equals null`; `$in: []` → `in []`; `$between` pair; `$contains 5`; `$icontains 'x'`; `$startsWith`; AST `['f','=',1]`, `['f','=',null]`, `IN`/`EQUALS`/`==`/not-equal-infix spellings, `is_null` with a filler value, `contains ''`, `between [1,2]`; `{}` → `[]`. Identity by reference (no notice): `[]`, any rule array (alias operators included), `{ f: null }`, `$null`/`$exists`, `$in` with `null`/boolean members, `$eq` array, `$between [1]`, `$icontains ''`, `$text`, `$OR`, unknown/mis-cased ops, all-or-nothing rows, field references, `like`, scalar `in`, 4-tuples, `and`/`or` groups (also uppercase), `[[[...]]]`, string/number/null filters. Registry fixture: 4 notices, `after` reproduced exactly, second replay same reference and 0 notices. §1-§5 of the test pin the same and pass locally (3 files, 222 tests).
- **Lossless against the wire path at the objectui pin `f8a9d0fb`: right.** Both shapes reach one lowering: `toFilterNode`/`mergeFilterNodes` (`packages/core/src/utils/filter-converter.ts:1297-1318`) for the binding and the grid, and the adapter's `translateFilterToAST` (`packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts:647-660`, which sends records through the same `convertFiltersToAST`) for the blocks that hand `$filter: schema.filter` raw (kanban `:681`, calendar `:727`, map `:914`, tree `:753`, timeline `:405`, gantt `:865`, record_picker `:135`); `element:number` goes through `lowerAnalyticsFilterForWire` (`:690-720`), which passes a record through and lowers an array via `parseFilterAST`. Probe: `{ a: 1, b: { $gte: 2, $lte: 3 } }` lowers to `{ $and: [{a:1},{b:{$gte:2}},{b:{$lte:3}}] }` from both forms. `null` decline matches `convertFiltersToAST:531-534`.
- **NOT lossless on the pin's in-memory path — WRONG (blocking, see verdict).** `ValueDataSource.find` (`packages/core/src/adapters/ValueDataSource.ts:1093-1105`) reads an OBJECT `$filter` through `matchesFilter` (`:905`, the record dialect) but an ARRAY `$filter` through `matchesASTFilter` (`:564-597`), whose head must be a string or an array: a rule object is refused by `refuseFilterNode` (`:70-73`: "Rows are excluded rather than passed through", console.warn) so EVERY row is excluded. At the pin four of the twelve doors hand `schema.filter` unlowered to a `ValueDataSource` built from inline data: `object-map` (`plugin-map/src/ObjectMap.tsx:831-833`, `hasInlineData && dataProvider === 'value'`), `object-tree` (`plugin-tree/src/ObjectTree.tsx:835-837`), `object-calendar` (`plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx:645-647`), `object-gantt` (`resolveDataSource` → `ValueDataSource` for `provider: 'value'`, `resolveDataSource.ts:70`, then `adapter.find(resource, { $filter: schema.filter })` at `ObjectGantt.tsx:865`). objectui's own pin lowers first precisely because of this (`ValueDataSource.astFilterVocabulary.test.ts:306-312`: `toFilterNode([{ field, operator: 'equals', … }])` before `find`). So a stored `object-map`/`tree`/`calendar`/`gantt` block with `data: { provider: 'value', items }` and a record `filter: { status: 'active' }` renders filtered rows today and renders NO rows once the row is converted at rest. The PR body's seam reading ("`toFilterNode` / `mergeFilterNodes` … so a stored row served as the rule array renders") stops one function short. The ruling excluded C "on the fault axis alone" because it "silently changes what some pages select"; this is the same fault class on a narrower population, and the dev applied exactly this standard to decline `null` values.
- **Reach = 12 doors.** §6 derives the door set from `ComponentPropsMap` (every type whose `filter`/`defaultFilters` refuses a record with the rule-array prescription) and holds `RULE_ARRAY_FILTER_BLOCK_TYPES` (`registry.ts:10306-10317`) and `RULE_ARRAY_DEFAULT_FILTERS_BLOCK_TYPES` (`:10324`) equal to it; the binding is on every component (`ui/page.zod.ts:395`), the only `ElementDataSourceSchema` holder. The named entry's own body already lists `element:number`/`record_picker` doors among the seven (card #17320 table) and the `defaultFilters` entry shares helper, record form and table; the widening is a defensible reading of "the family" and the dev declared it (PR body table + report deviation 3). Acceptable, with a word already given.
- **`retiredFromLoadPath: true` + step18 wiring: right.** All 35 `toMajor: 18` conversions at head are retired (35/35), ADR-0087 sanctions a retired conversion for a pre-launch break (`docs/adr/0087…md:383-385`), `migrations.test.ts:28-44` pins `conversionIds` ⊆ registry with matching major, `step18.conversionIds` gains the id (`migrations/registry.ts:5328`, hand-written region), and `applyConversions` iterates `ALL_CONVERSIONS` with no `PROTOCOL_MAJOR` gate, so the stored seam replays it now like its siblings (§7 pinned).
- **Public surface.** `isRecordForm` is now exported from `ui/filter-rule-array.ts:99` but that module is not re-exported by any entry; `ruleArrayFilterError` signature unchanged. No API-surface change; CI `Lint & Repo Gates` green.
- **Idempotence / identity / no flattening.** Probed above: rule arrays and `[]` identity by reference, second replay a no-op, combinator records and AST groups byte-identical with no notice.

### ② Semver level

`minor` for `@objectstack/spec` is right and matches the sibling D2-conversion changesets at head (`17053`, `17157`, `17260`: all `minor`). `Clause-②: no` is truthful: no accept set moves (no door schema in the diff; §7 pins the authoring funnel refuses as before), a conversion is added to the ledger as ruled. ADR-0087 prose made false was corrected in exactly the two entries that carried an at-rest claim (`18.element-data-source-…:60-77`, `18.object-grid-default-filters-…:51-59`); the two siblings carry none (grep). `migrations/registry.ts` generated regions (`:7829-7847`, `:10817-10825`) match the entry files and `check:migration-registry` is in the green `Lint & Repo Gates`; `docs/protocol-upgrade-guide.md` and `spec-changes.json` carry no step-18 entry yet (0 hits), so nothing published is stale. Head check-runs: 39 total, 33 success, 6 skipped (`Auto Label`, `Check PR Size`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Build Docs`, 2× opt-in tarball smoke), 0 failures.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Stopped TODO half, honest.** PR body (`Part of #17321`, "Stopped half" section), the changeset (`:52-53`), the entry prose (`18.element-data-source-…:76-77`) and the generated registry copy (`migrations/registry.ts:7845`) all say `os migrate meta --stored` does not list pass-through rows yet; the conversion `summary` and `step18.rationale` make no listing claim. `Part-of PR must not also close its card` check green.
- **`$null` / `$exists` declined although the pin maps them totally** (`filter-converter.ts:733-740`: `$null: v` → `is_null`/`is_not_null`, `$exists: v` → the inverse). Ruling item 1's letter ("operator object → the mapped operator") would cover them; the dev's "one table" narrowing is conservative, flagged in Acceptance notes. Not blocking.
- **Changeset sentence "`os migrate meta --from 17` lists the edits"** is true only with `--to 18` while `PROTOCOL_VERSION` is `17.0.0` (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/meta.ts:69,200-221` defaults `--to` to `PROTOCOL_MAJOR` and prints the wider-range hint); the same house sentence is in sibling step-18 changesets. Not blocking.
- **`.changeset/19514-…` "RE-SAVING it is refused" sentence** becomes partly stale for the converted forms; dev noted it, carrier none. Acceptable as noted.
- **`$`-prefixed non-combinator keys (`$text`)**: conversion declines any top-level `$` key (`registry.ts:10374`); the refusal still renders it as a field, which is what the pin does with it too (`convertFiltersToAST` treats it as a field). Unchanged from base; not this PR's to fix.
- **The blocking item above is the one boundary the author should have flagged**: the losslessness reading was against `toFilterNode`/`mergeFilterNodes` only; the in-memory `ValueDataSource` seam (the same file family the dev cited for the `null` decline) was not read.

The conversion is not lossless on the objectui pin's in-memory path: `ValueDataSource.find` (`f8a9d0fb` `packages/core/src/adapters/ValueDataSource.ts:1093-1105`, `:564-597`, `:70-73`) matches a record `$filter` but refuses a rule-object array and excludes every row, and `object-map` (`ObjectMap.tsx:831-833`), `object-tree` (`ObjectTree.tsx:835-837`), `object-calendar` (`ObjectCalendar.tsx:645-647`) and `object-gantt` (`ObjectGantt.tsx:661,865` via `resolveDataSource.ts:70`) hand `schema.filter` to it unlowered when the block carries `data: { provider: 'value', … }`. A stored block of those four types with inline data and a mappable record `filter` goes from filtered rows to no rows after the at-rest rewrite — the silent selection change the ruling excluded on the fault axis. Fix within the PR's file surface: decline the conversion for a component whose properties carry inline value data (the same all-or-nothing reasoning already used for `null`), pin it in §2, and state the exception in the entry prose and changeset; or, if the author argues this is objectui's defect to fix (its `ValueDataSource` has no rule-object arm), record the measured exception in the entry prose and changeset and name the objectui carrier before enqueue.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a0360aad8cdfb17203cb9c6ca7adab17c88dd3b3`

### ① Derived judgments

- **(a) Round-0 blocking item 1 is closed.** `rendersInlineRows` (`packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts:10496-10502`) answers true for `properties.data` that is an array, a dict with `provider === 'value'`, or any truthy `properties.staticData`; `apply` returns the component untouched before either door is read (`:10595`), so `dataSource.filter`, `properties.filter` and `properties.defaultFilters` all stay as stored on such a node. That set is exactly what the pin's ladder resolves to `provider: 'value'`: `resolveRecordSourceConfig` (`f8a9d0fb` `packages/core/src/utils/record-source.ts:284-306`) returns `data` verbatim when it is on the block's arm (`:172-176`: view-data = any truthy non-array, so `hasInlineData = provider === 'value'` in `ObjectMap.tsx:739`, `ObjectGantt.tsx:626`; undeclared = any truthy, `ObjectTree.tsx:593`) and wraps a truthy `staticData` as `provider: 'value'` (`:296-300`, the same truthiness test as `Boolean(staticData)`). The calendar's array arm returns a bare `data` array with no `provider`, so it never reaches the in-memory path (`ObjectCalendar.tsx:445-455`, `:498`, `:609`) and is inline only via `staticData`; the PR's bare-array decline is therefore a safe superset. Door by door at the pin: map (`ObjectMap.tsx:796`, `:831-833`), tree (`:796`, `:835-837`), calendar (`:609`, `:645-647`) and gantt (`:661` via `resolveDataSource.ts:70`, then `:865`) are the four that hand `schema.filter` unlowered to `ValueDataSource.find` (`ValueDataSource.ts:1089-1105`: array to `matchesASTFilter :564`, whose rule-object head falls to `refuseFilterNode :602`/`:70`), and each is declined by the shape it reads. Grid ignores `filter`/`defaultFilters` when `hasInlineData` (`ObjectGrid.tsx:1474`, `:1800-1811`, `:1848`); kanban and timeline use inline rows whole and send `filter` only on their fetch (`ObjectKanban.tsx:519`, `:681`, `:717`; `ObjectTimeline.tsx:254-256`, `:405`, `:420`, `:487`), so on those a decline changes nothing and a conversion would have changed nothing. Metric, `element:number` and `element:record_picker` have no inline-row path. The `api` arm is not in-memory anywhere (map `:930-933` and calendar `:745-747` refuse it; tree has no arm; gantt gets an `ApiDataSource`, see ③). **Probe** on a throwaway worktree of the head (removed after): 532 checks, 0 failures — every one of the 12 door types plus `page:card` / `record:related_list`, times 10 inline shapes (`data` value with/without `items`, bare/empty `data` array, `staticData` rows/`[]`/`{}`/string/number, value plus `staticData: null`): whole-chain output is the SAME REFERENCE, byte-identical, 0 notices, and `applyConversionsToStoredItem('page', …)` leaves the row equal; 12 bound shapes (no key, `provider: 'object'`, `staticData` null/false/0, `data` null/false, `provider: 'api'`, `provider: 'schema'`, string `data`, `data` without provider, mis-cased `provider: 'Value'`) convert the binding on every type, the block filter on the 10 family types and `defaultFilters` on the grid, with the exact notice count, and replay as a no-op. Nesting is right both ways (`walk.ts:286` calls the mapper first and then descends into the returned node's `properties`): a convertible child under an inline parent converts, an inline child under a bound parent stays. A slot-held inline component stays. Combinators stay.
- **(b) Decline-by-shape is safe and pinned.** A declined filter is the stored value the renderer already reads today, so it cannot change any selection; the only cost is fewer converted rows (grid/kanban/timeline with inline rows, and a bare `data` array on a view-data block, which the ladder would have ignored). §2 of the test pins 6 inline rows including `dataSource.filter` (`page-component-filter-record-to-rule-array.test.ts:261-289`), `defaultFilters` on an inline grid (`:291`), and the object-bound control on the same type (`:303`); the registry fixture gains an inline `object-map` row that stays identical with `expectedNotices` still 4 (`registry.ts:10660`, `:10735`, `:10769`). The dev's second ablation (decline removed, 9 red, clean restore) is the right direction.
- **(c) Round-0's other judgments still hold at this head.** Accept/refuse sets unchanged: no door schema is in the diff (8 files: the two registries, the new test, `ui/filter-rule-array.ts` message text plus `isRecordForm` export, its guidance test, two semantic entries, one changeset). Refusal text moves only for combinator records: `ui/filter-rule-array.ts` and its guidance test are byte-identical between `b1c9143f` and `a0360aad`, so round-0's 17-input measurement (14 identical, 3 combinator inputs changed, code and path fixed) stands. The mapper (`recordFilterToRules :10371`, `astFilterToRules :10404`, `legacyFilterToRuleArray :10461`, door-acceptance gate `:10466`, `$`-key guard `:10374`) is untouched by round 1, so the wire-path losslessness reading (`toFilterNode`/`mergeFilterNodes` `filter-converter.ts:1295`/`:1376`, `translateFilterToAST`) and the per-operator §4 pins stand. Identity and idempotence: probed above. `retiredFromLoadPath: true` (`:10569`), `apply.ts:132` skips it on the load path, `stored.ts:100` replays with `includeRetired: true`, `step18.conversionIds` carries the id (`migrations/registry.ts:5329`), §0 and §7 pin all of it; `applyMetaMigrations` defaults `toMajor` to `PROTOCOL_MAJOR` (`chain.ts:71`), so §7's explicit `17, 18` and its comment are about the library, not the CLI.
- Head check-runs at write time: 42 runs, 37 success, 5 skipped, 0 failing, 0 in progress (an earlier read had a `Check Changeset` re-run in progress; it completed green).

### ② Semver level

`minor` for `@objectstack/spec` is right and matches the sibling D2 changesets. `Clause-②: no` is truthful: no accept set moves, a conversion is added to the ledger, exactly as ruled. The inline-rows exception is stated consistently in the four places that must carry it: entry `18.element-data-source-and-object-block-filter-rule-array.ts:60-81` (the three shapes named, the four renderers named, the "does not list these rows yet" sentence kept), entry `18.object-grid-default-filters-rule-array.ts:51-59`, the hand-written `step18.rationale` (`migrations/registry.ts:5291`), the conversion `summary`/docblock, and the changeset (`:44-51`); the generated regions match the entry files (see ③). One prose nit, not false: the grid entry names "data with provider value, or staticData" and omits the bare `data` array the code also declines — the grid's published `data` row is the `ViewData` union whose bare array is converged by `object-grid-data-view-data-converged`, so on-contract grid rows have no such shape. **Round-0's nit is falsified on `origin/main` `cfe2387a`, as the dev says**: `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/meta.ts:88` `CHAIN_TERMINUS_MAJOR = Math.max(PROTOCOL_MAJOR, ...MIGRATION_MAJORS)` (18 while step18 exists), `:393` `toMajor = flags.to ?? CHAIN_TERMINUS_MAJOR`, the `--to` help at `:303-307`, pinned by `packages/cli/test/migrate-meta-default-range.test.ts` (#17134). That constant was already on main at the PR's merge-base `84880f92` (introduced 2026-09-22), so round-0 misread `:69` (docblock prose) and `:200-212` (the widening hint for an explicit narrower `--to`). The changeset's `os migrate meta --from 17` sentence (`:33`) is correct without `--to 18`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Stopped TODO half: honestly stated everywhere** — PR body (`Part of #17321`, "Stopped half" with the four sites), changeset `:51`, both entries (`:81` and the sibling), the conversion docblock; `Part-of PR must not also close its card` is green. The seat's partial-landing route (release with `pm:retriage`) is recorded on the card (`5852989736`).
- **Merge onto current `origin/main` (`cfe2387a`, moved twice during this review) is clean**: `git merge-tree --write-tree` exits 0 (tree `889f1b90`). Main added `18.cel-predicate-list-comparand-refused` and `18.rls-check-on-select-or-delete-policy-refused` and edited two other entries, all in disjoint hunks of `migrations/registry.ts`. Static reading of the merged tree, not a gate run: every non-comment line of all 249 semantic entry files is present in the merged `registry.ts`, the PR's id is in `conversionIds`, and `rendersInlineRows` is in the merged conversions registry — so `check:migration-registry` has nothing to regenerate. `PROTOCOL_VERSION` is still `17.0.0`, so no published upgrade-guide text is stale.
- **`provider: 'api'` on `object-gantt` (unmeasured, not blocking)**: the only `api` arm that sends `filter` anywhere is gantt's `ApiDataSource.find`, which JSON-stringifies `$filter` into a query param to the author's own URL (`ApiDataSource.ts:71-80`). After conversion that endpoint receives the rule array instead of the record. Whether it reads `$filter` at all, or in which dialect, is the endpoint's contract, not the platform's, and the spec already declares the rule array as the one form; no in-pin outcome is measurable, unlike `ValueDataSource`. The seat may widen the decline to `provider: 'api'` at the same shape site if it wants zero wire change on author URLs; the record does not require it.
- **The binding decline is a superset**: at the pin `dataSource.filter` reaches an inline-row renderer only through `ElementDataSourceGate`, which lowers both halves with `mergeFilterNodes` (`ElementDataSourceGate.tsx:341`, `:361`; a rule lowers to an AST tuple, `filter-converter.ts:1237`), and `plugin-tree` mounts no gate at all. So the at-risk stored shape is an inline-row map/tree/calendar/gantt with a record `properties.filter` and no binding; declining the binding too costs converted rows, never correctness. Fine as ruled-conservative.
- Carried, unchanged: `$null`/`$exists` declined though the pin maps them (Acceptance notes); `.changeset/19514-…` "re-saving is refused" partly stale for converted forms (noted, carrier none); `$text` rendered as a field by the worked rewrite (base behaviour). The `props` bag cannot mask inline rows: `PageComponentSchema` refuses it (`unrecognized_keys`, probed).
- The objectui carrier for `ValueDataSource` refusing a canonical rule array (the dev's round-1 probe: a spec-conformant filter already renders no rows on an inline-row map/tree/calendar/gantt) is the precondition for dropping this decline later; its filing is not verifiable from this review's allowed inputs.
- PR body checked against the head: 12 doors match `RULE_ARRAY_FILTER_BLOCK_TYPES` (`:10306-10317`) plus `defaultFilters` (`:10324`) plus the binding; "57 tests" matches the file (27 `it` sites, 35 table rows); the seam bullet and the "Left byte-identical" list now name the inline shapes and the four renderers with correct pin lines.
